log: `Dependencies` gains `requirementRegistry` (the module instance by default, `game.requirements` in `dependenciesFor`), so strategies can ask what the ruleset's things need and are made obsolete by in the game they play, e.g. whether a Wonder still does anything now that civ1-wonder's `isObsolete` reads the game's requirements (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
chore: CI compiles, formats and checks the committed output, as the other engine repos' does (civ-clone/web-renderer#66)

`Requirements.ts` declares the entries: the advance each improvement needs, the improvements a city needs any one of first (Bank, University, Power Plant) and the ones that stop it (Courthouse, Factory and the three plants), as `mode: 'any'`, `range: 'city'`. `registerRules` adds them to the game's `requirements`, which makes the build rules from them with `Rules/City/build`'s deriver: the same logic, items and place in registration order as before, so play is unchanged. The rules are named for the first time (civ-clone/web-renderer#24), under the entries' ids (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).

The not-built and Hydro Plant site rules stay written by hand, now named `civ1-city-improvement:city/build/not-built` and `civ1-city-improvement:city/build/hydro-plant-site`, each with an entry describing it through a `Condition`. `getRules` still returns every build rule, for rule registries without a game's `requirements`.
From the review: without Code of Laws the check passed whatever the excluded-by rule did.
chore: CI compiles, formats and checks the committed output, as the other engine repos' does (civ-clone/web-renderer#66)

New `Requirements.ts` holds an entry per government, `civ1-government:governments/availability/<Government>`: Despotism requires nothing, so it is always met, and Communism, Democracy, Monarchy and Republic each require their advance. `registerRules` adds them to `game.requirements` where the availability rules were always registered, and the deriver makes the same `Availability` rules as before, now under the entries' ids. Each entry is one alternative way to its government, since a player may take one by any rule that allows it (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
chore: the committed Governments.js.map matches its formatted source
chore: require core-game 0.1.14 and core-requirement 0.1.1

`Requirements.ts` declares the entries: every part needs the Apollo Program, built by anyone, and each part needs its advance. `registerRules` adds them to the game's `requirements`, which makes the build rules from them with `Rules/City/build`'s deriver: the same shape and the same place in registration order as before, so play is unchanged. The rules were unnamed and now have the entries' ids. The rule that a player's spaceship mustn't have launched stays written by hand, as `civ1-spaceship:city/build/not-launched`, with an entry naming it (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
`getRules` still returns every build rule, for rule registries without a game's `requirements`.

From the review: the Apollo Program counts for anyone because its entry is the world's, and an advance for the city's player because its entry is the player's, so a plugin changing a range changes play as well as the graph (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
chore: CI compiles, formats and checks the committed output, as the other engine repos' does (civ-clone/web-renderer#66)

`Requirements.ts` declares the entries: the advance each Wonder needs, Nuclear units needing the Manhattan Project built by anyone, and the advance that makes each Wonder obsolete once anyone discovers it (both `range: 'world'`). `registerRules` adds them to the game's `requirements`, which makes the build rules and the `Complete` rules that announce obsolescence from them, now named, in the same places in registration order, so play is unchanged. The once-only and Hoover Dam rules stay written by hand, now named too.

`isObsolete` reads the entries from the game's requirements (a new optional last argument, defaulting to the module registry), and `hasWonder`, `onWonderLandMass`, `pyramidsActive` and the rule factories pass the game's through, so a plugin's change to an entry reaches play. `obsoletedBy` is still exported, read from the entries (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).

From the review: the suites' helper added the obsolete entries to defaultGame's requirements, so a suite importing registerRules afterwards (as one process under ts-mocha) refused them as duplicates; the helper now imports registerRules, so the entries are there once. The build rules read whose Wonder or advance counts from the entry's range (anyone's for world, the city's player's otherwise), and an obsolete entry that isn't the world's is refused, as isObsolete reads only the world's (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).

`CityBuild#unavailable()` returns every item `available()` leaves out, with the ids of the rules that refused it (`null` for an unnamed one). A ruleset's requirement entries share their rules' ids, so an id names what is missing: the data for saying why a city can't build something (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
docs: unavailable() runs every applicable rule, unlike available()

`for(Subject)` reads the index by subject for the class and each class it extends, then puts them back in the order they were added, instead of filtering every entry. civ1-wonder's `isObsolete` reads the registry from yield and cost rules (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).

civ1-wonder's `isObsolete` now reads what makes a Wonder obsolete from the game's requirements, so `isUsefulWonder` passes the AI's `requirementRegistry` (base-strategy-ai 0.1.4's new dependency; the module registry, defaultGame's, for a client built by hand). The suite gives its own registry civ1-wonder's obsolete entries and passes it to the Wonder rule factories (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
